negative_findings.description: Searched in both Ukrainian and English for an adviser-maintained, structured compliance-DEADLINE TRACKER for Ukraine banking/payments (a calendar or table of 'rule → effective date → who is affected'). Nothing of that shape was found on any UA law firm or Big-4 Ukraine site.
negative_findings.result_summary: The closest artefact is PwC Ukraine's recurring 'Key NBU Changes in <month>' digest, which is prose segmented by regulated population rather than a dated tracker. All other firms publish episodic per-event alerts. Deadline information exists but must be extracted from prose.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The A3 workstream cannot inherit a ready-made deadline calendar from advisers; it must construct one by parsing effective-date statements out of alerts. This raises the extraction burden and makes the PwC digest disproportionately valuable as the single periodic anchor.

negative_findings.description: Checked whether the international firms covering Ukraine (CMS, Wolf Theiss, Baker McKenzie, Kinstellar) publish Ukrainian-language versions of their UA regulatory alerts.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only Kinstellar was observed publishing a genuinely paired UKR/ENG edition (the Payment Services Law newsletter PDFs). CMS, Wolf Theiss and Baker McKenzie output on Ukraine appeared English-only in every result seen. Among domestic firms, Asters and Sayenko Kharenko do maintain uk/en mirrors.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For uk-language terminology extraction the cell must lean on domestic firms (Asters, Sayenko Kharenko, Arzinger, INTEGRITES), PwC/KPMG Ukraine's uk trees and Kinstellar's paired PDFs; international firms are en-only signal and cannot anchor the glossary.

negative_findings.result_summary: Both returned HTTP 404. The homepage revealed the actual hub is https://sk.ua/uk/insights/ with a category filter ?cat=publications-uk, and article URLs are numeric IDs (sk.ua/uk/2937/) rather than slugs.

negative_findings.result_summary: No banking/payments regulatory alert pages for these firms surfaced in the queries run. Their existence as ranked UA firms is corroborated indirectly (rankings coverage), but no alert feed was observed, so none is recorded as a candidate.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Absence here is a search-coverage limitation, not proof these firms are silent — they are the natural next expansion set for this cell, best reached via the directory/ranking pointers rather than open web search.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell's confirmed adviser set is roughly a dozen firms; second-tier and boutique fintech/payments advisers (Aequo, Redcliffe Partners, Ilyashev, Eterna, Axon Partners, Juscutum and similar fintech-leaning boutiques) are unconfirmed. Boutiques are often faster than the majors on payment-institution licensing detail.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate firms from the Ukrainian Law Firms handbook plus Legal500/Chambers Ukraine banking-finance and fintech rankings, then check each firm's own publications page directly rather than relying on open web search.

coverage_gaps.description: Advisers increasingly push first-look commentary to LinkedIn and Telegram (a FinTech Ukraine Telegram channel surfaced during searching) before the firm website is updated. These channels were not systematically explored in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scope a separate pass over adviser LinkedIn pages and relevant UA fintech/legal Telegram channels, assessing ToS and collection legality per platform before any automated collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Confirmed adviser sources are strongest AFTER a rule is adopted. Coverage of the consultation/draft stage (проєкт постанови, громадське обговорення) rests mainly on one trade outlet (dtkt.ua) and occasional firm previews.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair this cell with the regulator-side cell (NBU draft-regulation and public-consultation pages) and use adviser alerts as interpretation rather than as the primary early-warning channel.

coverage_gaps.description: Older Baker McKenzie Ukraine legal alerts were only reachable via a third-party repost (USUBC), suggesting firm sites prune historical alerts. No firm was observed to offer a complete dated archive or RSS feed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Establish snapshot-on-first-sight collection immediately, and use Lexology/Mondaq/CEE Legal Matters plus web archives for historical backfill, accepting that pre-2022 adviser coverage will be incomplete.

coverage_gaps.description: The two highest-yield pointers (Lexology, Mondaq) and LIGA360 are all wall-protected to some degree, and all firm content is copyrighted client-alert material.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fix a metadata-only policy for aggregators and paywalled services (title, date, firm, URL, short abstract) and collect substantive text only from the originating firm's open page; document the policy before any crawler is built.

brief: Ukraine's banking/payments adviser layer is a genuinely strong bilingual bridge for workstream A3: domestic majors (Asters, Sayenko Kharenko, Avellum, Arzinger, INTEGRITES) publish dated client alerts that name the NBU resolution number and its effective date, and Asters, Sayenko Kharenko, PwC and KPMG maintain parallel uk/en trees, while Kinstellar's paired UKR/ENG payment-services PDFs are an unusually clean terminology bridge. The standout periodic source is PwC Ukraine's recurring 'Key NBU Changes in <month>' digest, which segments changes by regulated population (banks, financial companies, payment institutions, insurers, collectors) — no adviser in this cell publishes an actual structured deadline tracker, so dates must be parsed out of prose. Lexology and Mondaq are the most efficient discovery pointers into firms that never surface in general web search, but both are wall-protected and should be used for metadata only, with substantive collection done at the originating firm. The main weakness is lifecycle: advisers are excellent post-adoption interpreters and only occasionally flag drafts, so this cell should be paired with regulator-side consultation monitoring rather than treated as the early-warning channel.
